amazon.task: buy a physical product on Amazon: search for an item, work the results list, open and assess a product page (price, rating, variant options, delivery date), add to cart, and check out; complete when the order confirmation or the final checkout review screen with the order total is on screen. Surface pinned: Amazon's own website or app — not a third-party wrapper or assistive shopping app, not a haul/unboxing video, not a deals-roundup or affiliate-listicle without a live purchase session. Variants: returns and refunds (see returns), reordering a past purchase (see reorder), leaving a review (see review), and Amazon Fresh grocery orders (see groceries) do not belong.

banking.task: carry out an everyday banking task in a bank's own website or app (Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Capital One, a credit union): sign in, then complete one concrete arc — transfer money between accounts, deposit a check with the camera, or find and download/read a statement — through the bank's review-and-confirm step; complete when the bank's confirmation of the transfer or deposit (or the opened statement) is on screen. Surface pinned: the bank's own app or site — not p2p apps (Venmo/Cash App belong to the p2p domain), not budgeting apps, not crypto exchanges.

tree.label: Manage the bank account
tree.note: do 1 then 2, then the job the session is for: 3 then 4 to send money - 3 runs standalone first when the recipient is new (22Zy, 2NVw) and collapses to the pick at 4.3 when saved (60Qk); 5 to put money in; 6 to pull a statement or receipt; 7 to open a deposit. no keeper runs more than two jobs: 48jl runs 5 twice for two methods, 7-fw runs 6 twice (receipt, then statement), 22Zy chains 3 into 4. then 8 - and 8 reaches into 6.10 and 6.11 when the success screen offers the receipt (4bGB, 5RS4). 22Zy takes its baseline for 8.3 before 1 even starts, on the receiving bank's own site.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to utilize their personal, physical biometric data for quick and secure authentication.

Surface pinned: a flight-booking site or airline app — not an airport kiosk, not a travel vlog, not a points/miles explainer without a live booking session. mapnav.task: get directions to a specific place with an online map (Google Maps, Apple Maps, Waze): search the destination, pick a travel mode, review the route options (time, tolls, transit lines), and start navigation or read off the chosen route; complete when the chosen route with its ETA is on screen or turn-by-turn navigation has begun. Surface pinned: the map product itself — not dashcam or driving footage, not travel vlogs that happen to show a map.

tree.label: Navigate to a destination
tree.note: do 1 - five keepers start in the phone's settings and two install the app first. 2 floats: before any destination when the preference is the point (zJVt, HrMd, 4AhB, mo0Q), through the per-route door from inside 4 (obk4, bQbE, kIU1, lYnD), or never. then 3, then 4 - except on desktop, where 4.1's form comes first and 3 happens inside it (7EYu, bQbE, 60tT). rework 4 until the route reads right. then one of three endings: 5 (sixteen keepers start guidance, none arrives on camera), 6 (keep or hand off the route instead - 7EYu, 60tT, ETAP, VO5N, sWXu), or nothing (bQbE, FfFy, HrMd, kIU1, PjID). 7 and 8 are excursions from the main map (PjID, QULM, aGGT); 7.5 reruns 3 and 4 offline.

questions.why: The screen showed a ticket alert warning that the route requires a vignette, requiring a choice between adding the pass or bypassing the warning.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent automatically skips the vignette warning, you might drive on a toll road without the proper pass and receive a fine.

questions.question: How should I respond to the notification and data sharing prompts to start navigation?
questions.why: The app displays a series of pop-ups regarding notifications and data sharing that must be dismissed or accepted to access the active turn-by-turn navigation screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their privacy preferences regarding app notifications and navigation data sharing.

questions.question: Do you want to keep the navigation sound on, switch to alerts only, or mute it entirely?
questions.why: The Sound menu displays options for 'Sound on', 'Sound off', and 'Alerts only' to control the level of audio guidance during the trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might select an audio setting that either disrupts a quiet cabin or fails to provide the spoken directions you need.

questions.question: Do you want to inspect the route ahead for traffic and then re-center the map?
questions.why: Panning the map reveals a red section on highway '34' indicating traffic, and the 'Re-centre' button quickly snaps the view back to your current location.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the spatial awareness of exactly where the traffic delays are located along your journey.

questions.question: Which active trip settings, such as showing traffic on the map, do you want to enable?
questions.why: The expanded menu provides options to share your trip progress or display live traffic, which can help you stay informed during the drive.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personalize your active navigation view with specific overlays like live traffic or safety features.

questions.question: Do you want to review the entire route and alternative paths before re-centering?
questions.why: Checking the overview map allows you to evaluate the full 87-mile path and the alternative route labeled 'Similar ETA' before returning to active navigation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to visually inspect the entire route and decide if the alternative path better suits your driving preferences.

questions.question: Which Coles location do you want to add as a stop?
questions.why: The search results displayed multiple Coles locations with varying distances and detour times to choose from.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose the most convenient stop based on your personal preference for distance and detour time.

questions.question: Should you add this location as a new drive or as a stop on your current route?
questions.why: The screen shows buttons for 'New drive' and 'Add a stop', requiring a choice between replacing the existing itinerary or creating a multi-stop journey.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify whether they want to abandon their original destination or just make a detour along the way.

questions.question: Which specific map issue are you reporting?
questions.why: The screen displays a menu of map issues alongside a popup about a road closure on W 26th Ave, requiring you to categorize the problem.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to accurately categorize the navigation error based on your personal knowledge of the route.

questions.question: Which type of incident do you want to report on the map?
questions.why: The screen displays a menu of reportable incidents like crashes, speed cameras, and congestion to warn other drivers on the route.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to accurately report the specific real-world hazard you are currently seeing on the road.

questions.question: Do you want to access other apps like media or messages from the navigation dashboard?
questions.why: The driving mode dashboard displays icons for Calls, Messages, and Media, allowing you to use other phone features without leaving the navigation interface.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this to an agent means you lose the ability to seamlessly queue up your preferred media or check messages while the navigation runs.

questions.question: Do you want to answer or decline the incoming call?
questions.why: An incoming call banner with green and red buttons has appeared on the screen, requiring a choice that might interrupt your navigation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether this specific caller is important enough to speak with while you are driving.

questions.question: Do you want to authorize Waze to access your Spotify account?
questions.why: The screen displays an authorization prompt asking to connect Waze to Spotify for integrated music control.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to share your personal music streaming account data with the navigation app.

questions.question: Do you want to start playing music using the integrated Spotify widget?
questions.why: The screen displays a Spotify widget with playback controls, offering a way to manage audio without leaving the navigation view.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose the ability to decide whether and when to start your music during the drive.

questions.question: How do you proceed after reaching an intermediate stop?
questions.why: The screen shows options to rate the navigation or end the trip, requiring you to explicitly select 'Continue' to resume routing to your final destination.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to end the trip early at this stop or provide feedback on the navigation experience.

questions.question: Do you want to leave feedback on the navigation experience?
questions.why: The arrival screen displays a feedback prompt with smiley face icons to rate the trip before tapping 'Done'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might skip the rating or submit feedback that does not reflect your actual travel experience.

questions.question: How do you exit active navigation mode?
questions.why: Tapping the 'X' button stops the turn-by-turn guidance and returns you to the route overview screen showing the ETA and a Start button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to quickly cancel the active route if you need to change your plans or destination.

questions.question: Do you want to stop the automatic navigation?
questions.why: The screen indicates that navigation will start automatically and provides a 'Stop' button, requiring a decision on whether to begin the trip immediately.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to cancel the active turn-by-turn navigation if they were just checking the route and are not actually ready to leave.

children.label: Keep or hand off the route
children.note: any one of 6.1 to 6.6, each its own ending: print on desktop (7EYu, 60tT), a note link where the app has no save-route feature (ETAP), a planned drive (VO5N), a calendar entry left uncommitted (sWXu), a send-to-phone (sWXu). 6.6 is the save that bites back - Set home and go starts navigating by itself.

questions.question: Do you want to review the step-by-step distances on the printable directions page?
questions.why: The printable directions page displays detailed step-by-step instructions alongside specific leg and total distances for the trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to familiarize yourself with the specific distances of each leg before starting your journey.

questions.question: Should you add Street View images or map snippets to the printed directions for tricky turns?
questions.why: The print preview menu offers options to include a map or Street View image for individual steps, which helps familiarize the driver with important landmarks.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might default to printing text-only directions, depriving you of the visual landmarks you would have included for confusing intersections.

children.label: Save the route to a note

questions.question: Are you sure the saved link to 'Arnprior' includes your intermediate stops?
questions.why: The Quick Note link only mentions the final destination, which could incorrectly suggest that the intermediate stops to Carp and Galetta were not saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might see only the final destination in the link title and mistakenly discard it to rebuild the multi-stop route from scratch.

questions.question: How do you initiate the process of scheduling a future trip?
questions.why: The menu provides a 'Planned drives' option and a 'Plan a drive' button to help you determine when to leave based on anticipated traffic.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to manually plan the drive or connect your personal calendar and Facebook accounts for automatic event syncing.

questions.question: Do you see that the estimated drive time changed from 15 to 16 minutes after saving?
questions.why: The route preview showed a 15-minute drive to arrive at 5:00 PM, but the saved planned drives list displays a 16-minute drive.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might just pass along the initial estimate without noticing the system updated the travel time in the final saved list.

children.label: Add the route to the calendar

questions.question: Do you want to save this planned route to your calendar?
questions.why: The screen displays the detailed transit schedule and arrival times, which can be exported to trigger helpful departure alerts.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to integrate the trip into your personal schedule for automated reminders.

questions.question: Should you check the box to create a short URL for sharing this route?
questions.why: The screen displays a share pop-up with a long URL and a 'Short URL' checkbox, allowing you to customize the link format.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to share a concise version of the route link or just proceed to the schedule explorer.

questions.question: Which device or method should you choose to send the route to your phone?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Send to your phone' popup with multiple options, including specific connected devices, an email address, and a phone number for texting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might send the directions to an old device or an unchecked email address instead of the smartphone you actually have with you.

questions.question: Is this the correct location to save as your home?
questions.why: The screen shows a location pin and a 'Set home and go' button, making it important to verify the address before saving it as a permanent shortcut.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might save an inaccurate location as your home, which would permanently affect the routing for any future trips to this destination.

questions.question: Do you want to save this location to your favorites?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Favorites' menu with an 'Add new favorite' option, which lets you save frequently visited places for quicker access in the future.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might clutter your saved places with a one-time destination or miss the opportunity to save a place you visit often.

children.label: Use the maps offline
children.note: 7.1 then 7.2; 7.3 for what is already downloaded. 7.4 then 7.5 to prove the download works - PjID and QULM both stage the outage on purpose. 7.6 when the proof fails. 7.5 reruns 3 and 4 in miniature against the downloaded area.

questions.question: Do you need to access your profile settings or offline maps before starting your search?
questions.why: The profile icon in the top right corner provides access to additional app features like offline maps that could be necessary for your journey.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to proactively download offline maps or adjust account settings before navigating.

questions.question: Do you want to download a new offline map area or use one of the currently saved maps?
questions.why: The screen displays existing downloaded maps with their storage sizes and expiration dates, along with an option to select a new map area.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manage your device's storage space and decide exactly which geographic areas need to be available offline.

questions.question: How large of an area do you want to download for offline use?
questions.why: Adjusting the blue bounding box changes the map coverage and increases the required storage space from 30 MB to 80 MB.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to balance the offline map coverage area against the storage space it consumes on your device.

questions.question: Do you want to download this map area for offline use and consume up to 80 MB of your storage?
questions.why: The screen displays a prompt asking to confirm the download of the selected map area, noting it will use up to 80 MB of free space.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might approve the download without knowing if you have enough device storage or cellular data to spare.

questions.question: Are you okay with the downloaded offline map taking up more storage space than initially estimated?
questions.why: The screen initially estimated the offline map would use up to 80 MB, but later showed the downloaded file taking up 108 MB.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to monitor their device storage accurately when the agent fails to notice that a download exceeded its estimated size.

questions.question: Do you want to update the downloaded map before it expires?
questions.why: The screen indicates that the downloaded map will expire on June 5, 2023, unless it is updated.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to use your device's data and storage to keep this specific offline map current.

questions.question: Should you delete any existing offline maps to free up space?
questions.why: The screen displays a previously downloaded 49 MB map, and removing it can free up device storage before saving a new area.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over your device's storage management and the choice of which old maps to keep or discard.

questions.question: How do you simulate being offline to test the downloaded map?
questions.why: The Android quick settings panel displays active network connections like Wi-Fi that must be toggled off to ensure the app relies solely on downloaded data.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the map will successfully provide directions without an active internet connection.

questions.question: Does the destination shown on the screen match the one you stated you are routing to?
questions.why: The audio claims to route to a gas station, but the screen shows a failed route to High Falls followed by a new search for Genesee Brew House.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses accurate destination tracking if the agent relies on the spoken intent rather than noticing the actual on-screen routing failures and changes.

questions.question: Do you want to proceed with this offline route without live traffic data?
questions.why: The screen displays an offline icon and 'No traffic data', meaning the 15-minute estimate cannot account for current road conditions or delays.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to find an internet connection for live traffic updates or to delay the trip until real-time data is available.

questions.question: Since offline routing from your current location failed, what starting point should you select instead?
questions.why: The screen showed a 'No routes found in your offline maps' error, requiring you to choose a new origin within the downloaded area to successfully calculate a route.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to troubleshoot offline map limitations by manually selecting an alternative starting point.

children.label: Share your live location
children.note: 8.1, then 8.2 to 8.4 in the sheet's order; 8.5 fires mid-flow when the platform demands background access; 8.6 closes the loop. QULM runs all of it; aGGT opens the sheet and backs out.

questions.question: How long do you want to share your real-time location, and who should I send it to?
questions.why: The screen provides options to set a specific duration for location sharing and lists various messaging apps and contacts to send the link to.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent decides this, it might share your live location with the wrong contact or leave it running indefinitely, compromising your privacy.

questions.question: Do you need to share your current location with someone?
questions.why: The 'Your Location' bottom sheet provides options like 'Share location' and 'Save parking' that are useful for coordinating with others.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to proactively send their exact coordinates to a friend they are coordinating with.

questions.question: Do you want to share your real-time location?
questions.why: The app offers to share your continuous location with others across Google services, which updates even when the app is not in use.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally decide whether your continuous, real-time whereabouts are broadcasted to others.

questions.question: How long do you want to share your real-time location?
questions.why: The screen provides options to share your location for a set time, such as one hour, or indefinitely until turned off, which directly affects your privacy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to strictly control the duration of your location sharing, potentially exposing your whereabouts longer than intended.

questions.question: Which app do you want to use to share the location link?
questions.why: The screen shows a sharing menu with multiple communication apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, and Messages to choose from.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide which specific messaging platform is used to send your location to others.

questions.question: Who should receive your live location link?
questions.why: The WhatsApp 'Select contacts' screen requires you to choose a recipient from your recent chats to send the live location link to.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to safely select your own number to test the feature without broadcasting your location to other contacts.

questions.question: Are you comfortable sharing your name, photo, and real-time location via a link, and do you want to suppress this warning in the future?
questions.why: The app explicitly warns that anyone with the generated link will be able to see your personal details and live location, requiring you to accept this privacy risk to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate the privacy implications of broadcasting your live location and to decide whether to keep future warnings enabled.

questions.question: How do you open the shared live location?
questions.why: Tapping the provided Maps link in the WhatsApp chat directly opens the shared location in the map application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the seamless transition from their messaging app directly to the exact coordinates shared by their contact.

patientportal.task: use a patient portal (MyChart, FollowMyHealth, LabCorp or Quest portals, a health system's own portal): sign in and complete one concrete arc — view test results, read or send a message to the care team, view or download a visit summary or medical record, or check in for an upcoming visit; complete when the result, message, or record is on screen. Surface pinned: the portal itself — not symptom research (healthinfo), not appointment booking (doctor), not pharmacy refills (refill).

tree.label: Use the patient portal
tree.note: do 1 - 1.2 once, on a first invitation (L1Mf); 1.3 thereafter. then 2, and from 2 whichever of 3 to 6 the day's task is - each keeper walks one to three, none walks all four. 7 after any commit: 3.13, 5.9, 5.10.4, and 6.5 all hand into it. 4 gates on 3 at some clinics (CkVD: eCheck-In must complete before joining) and not others (fW6G: abandoned with Finish later, and the visit proceeds). 8 as needed and at the end.

children.label: Get into the portal
children.note: 1.1 where the portal is reached through the clinic's site or an email (FE1_, L1Mf). 1.2 replaces 1.3 on the invited first run and hands straight into the session. otherwise 1.3, with 1.4 as the browser interjects. FE1_ runs 1.3 twice by design - it signs out mid-demo and back in.

questions.question: Should you allow the app to send you notifications?
questions.why: The system prompts you to allow or deny notifications, which include alerts and badges that can notify you of upcoming appointments.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control whether this medical app is allowed to interrupt you with push notifications on your personal device.

questions.question: Should you allow the app to access your camera for video visits?
questions.why: The app displayed a system prompt requesting camera access to enable video visits with your provider.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to grant a health app access to their device's camera.

questions.question: Which portal tab should you select to view a different history of lab results?
questions.why: The browser displays multiple tabs for different patient portals, so you must identify which one contains the specific lab history you need.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might click into the wrong portal and retrieve an incomplete or incorrect set of lab results.

questions.question: What is the exact web address you use to access the portal?
questions.why: The screen showed the address bar with 'mycarecorner.net', highlighting the importance of using the '.net' extension instead of a traditional '.com'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the specific knowledge of the correct domain extension needed to access their patient portal securely.

children.label: Register from the invitation
children.note: 1.2.1 to 1.2.4 in order - the code and the verification answer both come from the same email-and-form loop. then 1.2.5 and 1.2.6: two separate consent gates after the account already exists.

questions.question: How do you proceed to your health record once access is approved?
questions.why: The screen confirms you have completed the necessary steps to exchange information, but you must manually navigate to the home screen to see your record.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses the explicit confirmation that they have successfully completed the steps to exchange information with their provider.

questions.question: Which link should you click to begin the registration process?
questions.why: The email provides a specific URL and mentions an invitation code required to set up your new portal account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss seeing the exact instructions and invitation code sent directly by your healthcare provider.

questions.question: Which link in the signup email should you click to activate your account?
questions.why: The email contains a specific, time-sensitive link that must be clicked within 24 hours to access the portal and create your account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify the sender's address and ensure the activation link is a legitimate portal URL rather than a phishing attempt.

questions.question: Is the required identity code correctly entered so you can submit it?
questions.why: The screen shows an auto-filled identity code required to transfer your health information to MyCareCorner, which needs to be verified before submission.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the assurance of personally verifying that the correct security code from your private communications was used to access your sensitive health data.

questions.question: Are you entering the correct verification code to complete enrollment with this practice?
questions.why: Entering the 4-digit code from your messages confirms your identity and finalizes your enrollment with The Sound Pain Alliance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means an agent would need access to your personal text messages to retrieve the verification code and authorize access to your medical records.

questions.question: Are you ready to submit the registration form and create your account?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Create Account' button, indicating that the registration details are ready to be submitted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review their personal information for accuracy before the account is finalized.

questions.question: What personal information will you provide to create your account?
questions.why: The registration form requires sensitive details like your date of birth, sex, and email address to establish your health portal identity.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose control over exactly which optional fields, like the profile image, are skipped or filled with your personal data.

questions.question: What personal information must you provide to verify your identity?
questions.why: The portal requires answering a specific security question, such as your date of birth, to confirm your identity and proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires sharing sensitive personal information, like your date of birth, with an agent to pass the security check.

questions.question: Are you ready to submit the verification answer?
questions.why: Submitting the correct security answer is required to bypass the verification prompt and access your health account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally handle their security questions, requiring them to share sensitive verification answers with the agent.

questions.question: Which record do you want to authorize for data transfer, and do you consent to the requested access?
questions.why: The screen requires selecting a specific patient record and granting the hospital permission to view and change your health information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to review the requested permissions and make an informed decision about sharing their health data.

questions.question: Should you agree to the practice consent form?
questions.why: The screen presents a consent form outlining the risks and conditions of using secure messaging and viewing medical records.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent accepts legal terms and conditions regarding medical communication risks on your behalf without your direct review.

questions.question: Do you agree to the terms of use to continue?
questions.why: The screen requires you to accept a long Terms of Use Agreement before you can proceed into the patient portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the chance to review how the portal handles your sensitive health data before legally agreeing to their terms.

questions.question: Do you want to sign in using the pre-filled credentials?
questions.why: The email and password fields are already populated with saved credentials, so you must decide whether to accept them or enter different information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify exactly which account is being accessed before the agent submits the saved login details.

questions.question: Has your session timed out?
questions.why: The Labcorp OnDemand login page displays a banner stating you have been logged out due to inactivity.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that their session expired and they must re-authenticate to access their health information.

questions.question: Should you allow the browser to save your login credentials for this site?
questions.why: The screen showed a Google Chrome prompt asking whether to save the password for the patient portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: A person delegating to an agent loses the ability to decide whether their sensitive health portal credentials are saved in the browser.

children.label: Find the task
children.note: 2.1, then 2.2 past whatever the feed stacks on top, then 2.3 for visit tasks - the other destinations open from the nav or a widget, and their entry ops sit in their own goals. re-entered between tasks: FE1_ returns here after each subtask, g18A comes back through Home to reach the inbox.

questions.question: Which section of the portal do you want to navigate to?
questions.why: The dashboard menu offers multiple paths like Health Record, Messaging, and Appointments, requiring you to select the one that matches your current goal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this navigation means you lose the ability to personally browse your available health categories and prioritize what information to review.

questions.question: Do you want to view your upcoming appointments or request a new one?
questions.why: The expanded Appointments menu offers distinct paths for checking your existing schedule versus initiating a new visit request.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice prevents you from deciding whether to review your current schedule or initiate a request for a new visit.

questions.question: Are there new results on the dashboard, or do you need to click to view all past records?
questions.why: The dashboard states there are no new results to view, meaning you must navigate to the full history to find older reports.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate reassurance of seeing that they have no new or unread test results pending.

questions.question: Do you want to review your account overview on the dashboard before navigating to your specific task?
questions.why: The dashboard displays immediate updates like upcoming appointments, current medications, and latest statements that might need your attention.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to catch important incidental updates about your health or billing that are surfaced on the main dashboard.

questions.question: Do you want to learn more about the hello2healow audio and video call feature before proceeding?
questions.why: The portal displays an interstitial promoting a new telehealth communication tool with options to learn more or skip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses the opportunity to learn about a potentially useful telehealth feature if the agent automatically dismisses the announcement.

questions.question: Should I dismiss the tutorial overlay about managing appointments?
questions.why: The screen displays a tutorial overlay explaining the appointments section, which must be dismissed to navigate the rest of the portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss the chance to read the platform's introductory guidance on how to manage your upcoming appointments and alerts.

questions.question: Which dashboard option do you select to find your upcoming tele-visit?
questions.why: The main screen features a circular menu with multiple options like 'Appointments', 'Check-in', and 'My Records', requiring a choice based on your specific goal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss seeing the layout of your health dashboard and any notification badges that indicate items needing your attention.

questions.question: Which appointment are you selecting to start your televisit?
questions.why: The screen lists your upcoming appointments, requiring you to identify the correct provider, date, and time to ensure you join the right session.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss the chance to personally verify the provider and schedule details before entering the virtual waiting room.

children.label: Check in for the visit
children.note: 3.1 opens it. then the verify stages in the order the clinic fixes, each closed by its own this-information-is-correct gate: iEZR runs 3.2, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7 to 3.9, 3.11, then 3.12; jNEa runs 3.3, 3.4, 3.6 to 3.11, then 3.12 three times over; CkVD shows only 3.6 before the video cuts. 3.13 ends it - or Finish later abandons it at any stage (fW6G, at 3.2).

questions.question: Do you want to import the reviewed questionnaire responses into the patient's chart?
questions.why: The screen displays the patient's submitted interim history with options to import, mark as reviewed, or reject the data.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally verify the patient's submitted answers before adding them to the official medical record.

questions.question: How much of your outstanding balance and copay do you want to pay today?
questions.why: The check-in screen presents options to pay just the $5.00 copay, the full $195.00 balance, or to pay later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means losing control over your immediate cash flow and how your medical debts are prioritized.

questions.question: Is this text message for the correct appointment, and what action should you take?
questions.why: The text message specifies it is for Shannon's appointment at Rainbow Pediatric Center, so you must verify this matches the intended patient and visit before clicking the link to begin check-in.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to personally verify that the check-in link corresponds to the correct patient and appointment details before proceeding.

questions.question: Are the displayed appointment details correct before you begin check-in?
questions.why: Reviewing the date, time, provider, and location ensures you are checking in for the correct upcoming visit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally catch any scheduling errors regarding your provider, time, or location before proceeding with the check-in.

questions.question: Is your pre-filled contact information correct?
questions.why: The portal displays your current address, phone numbers, and email, giving you the chance to verify or edit them before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to catch and correct outdated contact details in your medical record.

questions.question: Is your personal and contact information accurate as listed?
questions.why: The portal asks you to verify your address, phone number, and demographic details before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to update missing or outdated personal details, such as your gender identity or phone number.

questions.question: Do you want to add a new emergency contact, or does the current list look good?
questions.why: The portal asks you to review your emergency and PHI disclosure contacts, offering options to add a new one or confirm the existing list.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to designate a new trusted individual to receive emergency updates or discuss their medical information.

questions.question: Do you agree to the terms and billing policies of the telehealth visit?
questions.why: The screen presents a TeleVisit Consent Form detailing terms, risks, and billing policies that require your explicit acceptance to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent automatically accepts the form, you lose the chance to understand the telemedicine policies, technical risks, and billing information you are legally bound to.

questions.question: Do you agree to the financial policy?
questions.why: The portal requires you to review and sign the financial policy to establish a mutual financial understanding before proceeding with your care.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means an agent signs a legally binding financial agreement on your behalf without you reviewing the specific terms.

questions.question: How will you provide the required images of your insurance card?
questions.why: The screen prompts you to capture front and back images of your insurance card to verify your coverage for the visit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot physically use your device's camera to take pictures of your actual insurance card.

questions.question: How do you want to e-verify your tax return?
questions.why: The screen requires you to choose an identity verification method to finalize your submission, offering options like an Aadhaar-linked OTP, a Digital Signature Certificate, or an EVC.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide means they might choose a verification method that requires access to a specific device or digital certificate you cannot easily provide.

questions.question: What is the 6-digit OTP sent to your Aadhaar-registered mobile number?
questions.why: The screen requires the OTP sent to your Aadhaar-registered mobile number to verify your identity and authorize the tax return submission.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires sharing a time-sensitive, highly secure government verification code with a third party.

questions.question: What location will you enter as the place of filing for your tax declaration?
questions.why: The preview and submit screen requires a legally binding declaration and a specific filing location to proceed to validation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally attest to the accuracy of your return and explicitly state your filing location.

questions.question: Do you want to temporarily change the filing method to 'File by mail' to preview the full tax return PDF before submitting?
questions.why: The screen defaults to 'E-file', but changing the method to 'File by mail' allows you to generate and review the full PDF of your return before officially submitting or paying.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally review the completed tax forms line-by-line for accuracy before the agent officially submits the return.

questions.question: Are you absolutely sure you want to submit this return, knowing it cannot be modified?
questions.why: The screen warns that once you submit the return, you can no longer modify the details, making this your final chance to correct any errors.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final opportunity to personally verify your tax information before it is permanently locked and submitted to the government.

questions.question: Has your return been successfully filed and verified?
questions.why: Seeing the success message confirms your tax return was officially submitted and shows which contact methods will receive processing updates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss the immediate reassurance of seeing the final success screen and verifying the exact contact details where processing notifications will be sent.
